articles.title: The Card That Says “Wait for One Another”
articles.titleZh: 那张写着“彼此等候”的卡片
articles.summary: The parish meal has to begin at 6:15, six food-bank volunteers cannot arrive until 6:35, and evening prayer begins at 7:30. Marta and Thomas both want to avoid leaving late arrivals outside the shared meal: she favors waiting for everyone, while he proposes starting on time and holding food. After rereading 1 Corinthians 11 and checking records from ten years earlier, they do not change the text; they change how this contemporary parish applies “Wait for one another (1 Cor. 11:33)” to its common meal.
articles.summaryZh: 堂区六点十五分必须开饭，六名食物银行志愿者六点三十五分才能到，七点半还有晚祷。玛尔塔和托马斯都不想让晚到的人被落下：一个坚持全体等候，一个主张先开饭并留餐。重读林前11章和十年前记录后，他们改变的不是经文，而是当前堂区如何把“彼此等候（林前11:33）”落实成共同用餐。
storyParagraphs: Evening prayer was scheduled for 7:30 on Friday, and the Catholic parish hall had to start serving dinner at 6:15 or the children would not finish eating and the choir would not have time to clear the tables. But six food-bank volunteers could not finish work until 6:35. Dinner coordinator Marta was used to waiting until everyone had arrived before ringing the bell. Kitchen coordinator Thomas argued instead for beginning at 6:15 and keeping six complete meals warm. An old card clipped beside the door carried only the words: “Wait for one another (1 Cor. 11:33).”

Neither of them wanted the late arrivals to be left out. Marta worried that they would come in after everyone else was already halfway through the meal and people were already beginning to clear the tables. Thomas saw the other side: the children were hungry, the soup sat on the warmer, and every month the six volunteers entered saying, “Sorry for making everyone wait.” His first workflow note said, “Keep six meals in the kitchen; late shift eats when they arrive.” Marta thought that this solved the shortage of food but could still leave the six people apart from the main table.

At the volunteers’ meeting on Wednesday, they first opened the dinner records from ten years earlier to see how “wait until everyone arrives before ringing the bell” had become the practice. The records showed that there had been only one dinner sitting and that kitchen, food-distribution, and choir volunteers usually arrived before 6:00. Eating together had genuinely helped newcomers avoid sitting alone, but no entry treated 6:00—or waiting for the very last person—as a time fixed by the biblical text itself. Thomas placed the current rota beside it: by 6:15, families were already seated, while the six food-bank volunteers did not finish until 6:35.

They then reread the surrounding material in 1 Corinthians 11, including the discussion of divisions in the gathering and the fact that some people ate first while others went hungry. Both understood that Paul’s ancient Corinthian gathering was not a timetable for a modern Catholic parish dinner. But the surrounding passage changed how they viewed Thomas’s workflow note: simply keeping six meals in the kitchen could still leave the late shift eating apart from the main table. Thomas crossed out that line and replaced it with: “Reserve six seats in the hall; keep six meals warm; when the late shift arrives, someone eats with them.”

During the first trial, Marta led the shared blessing at 6:15 as usual and then serving began. Six places were kept open beside the main table, and six portions of every dish were reserved. Thomas and another volunteer stayed in the kitchen to finish up and did not sit down first. At 6:35, the six food-bank volunteers came in and went directly to the reserved seats; Thomas brought his own plate over and sat with them. Clearing began before 7:00, and evening prayer went ahead at 7:30.

The following Wednesday, the group had only one trial to look at and did not treat it as settled. On the next month’s rota, two of the late-shift volunteers had changed and the expected finish time was listed as anywhere from 6:25 to 6:40, so the group decided to extend the arrangement for a three-month trial. Before Friday evening prayer, Marta took down the card by the door and wrote a date on the back, followed by: “6:15 blessing; reserve seats for late shift; three-month trial.” The front still read, “Wait for one another (1 Cor. 11:33).” She clipped the card back in its original place.
storyParagraphsZh: 这个天主教堂区周五晚上七点半有晚祷，六点十五分堂区大厅必须开始开饭，否则孩子吃不完、唱经班也来不及收桌。可食物银行的六名志愿者要到六点三十五分才收工。晚餐负责人玛尔塔一直习惯等所有人到齐再敲铃；厨房负责人托马斯则主张六点十五分先开饭，把六份完整餐食保温留下。门边夹着一张旧卡片，正面只写着“彼此等候（林前11:33）”。
两人都不想让晚到的人被落下。玛尔塔担心他们进门时，别人已经吃完一半、桌上开始散；托马斯则看见孩子饿着、汤一直保温，那六个人每月进门第一句话都是“对不起，让大家等了”。他最初在流程纸上写的是“六份留厨房，晚班到后再吃”；玛尔塔觉得这样虽然不缺饭，却仍可能把六个人留在主桌之外。
周三志愿者会上，两人先翻十年前的晚餐记录，想弄清“全员到齐才敲铃”是怎么来的。记录显示，当时只有一轮晚餐，厨房、食物分发和唱经班的人通常六点前都到齐；“一起开饭”确实让新来的人不会独坐，但没有哪一页把六点或“必须等最后一个人”写成经文本身的固定要求。托马斯把现在的排班表摊在旁边：六点十五分家庭已经坐下，六点三十五分那六人才结束工作。
接着他们重读《哥林多前书》11章前后内容，其中谈到聚会中的分裂，也写到有人先吃、有人挨饿。两人都清楚保罗面对的古代哥林多聚会不是现代堂区周五晚餐时间表，但这段上下文让他们重新看托马斯那张流程纸：只把六份留在厨房，仍可能让晚班的人在主桌之外单独吃。托马斯把那一行划掉，改成“六席留大厅；六份保温；晚班到后有人同桌”。
第一次试行时，玛尔塔六点十五分照常带大家做共同祝福，然后开始盛汤。主桌旁留着六个座位，每道菜预留六份；托马斯和另一名志愿者在后厨收尾，没有先坐下。六点三十五分，食物银行组六个人进门，直接坐进预留的位置，托马斯也端着自己的盘子过去。七点前开始收桌，七点半晚祷照常进行。
下周三，小组只看了一次试行，没有把它当成定案。下个月排班表上，晚班志愿者换了两人，预计结束时间也写成六点二十五到六点四十之间，大家决定把安排延长试三个月。周五晚祷钟响前，玛尔塔取下门边卡片，在背面写上日期和一句“6:15祝福；为晚班留席；试行三个月”。正面的“彼此等候（林前11:33）”没有改，她把卡片夹回原处。
explanationParagraphs: Theological hermeneutics concerns how religious texts, doctrines, and traditions are understood and brought into the life of a community. Responsible interpretation usually considers language and genre, historical setting, literary context and related texts, interpretive tradition, communal practice, the interpreter’s present situation, and the consequences of a proposed application. It is neither mechanical execution of an isolated sentence nor simply interpreting the text however one wishes.

This story is explicitly about one contemporary Catholic parish reading 1 Corinthians 11; it does not imply that all Christian or other religious communities follow the same interpretive norms. The parish treats “Wait for one another (1 Cor. 11:33)” as a normative reference for its common meal while openly acknowledging that Paul’s ancient Corinthian gathering and a modern Friday parish dinner are not the same historical or liturgical setting. The new arrangement therefore has to account for the larger textual context, the conditions that produced the older parish practice, the present situation, and the practical consequences, while remaining open to further testing.
explanationParagraphsZh: 神学诠释关注宗教文本、教义和传统如何被理解并进入共同体生活。负责的解释通常需要考虑文本语言与文体、历史处境、上下文和其他相关文本、解释传统、共同体实践、解释者当下处境，以及某种应用会产生什么后果。它既不等于把孤立句子机械执行，也不等于个人想怎样理解就怎样理解。
这篇故事明确以一个当代天主教堂区阅读《哥林多前书》11章为例，不代表所有基督教或其他宗教采用同一套诠释规范。堂区把“彼此等候（林前11:33）”作为共同用餐的规范性参照，同时公开承认保罗面对的古代哥林多聚会与现代周五晚餐并非同一历史和礼仪场景；新安排因此必须说明文本上下文、旧实践形成条件、当前处境与实际后果，并保持可继续检验。
articles.overallZh: 这不是一个与经文无关的排班折中。两种最初读法都试图避免把人落在后面；真正改变方案的是，旧记录说明“全员到齐”来自过去同步到达的条件，而林前11章关于分裂、先吃和挨饿的上下文又让“六份留厨房”显得不够。因此新实践保留经文参照，却公开承认其历史差异和试行边界。
articles.overall: This is not merely a scheduling compromise unrelated to the text. Both initial readings try to prevent people from being left out. The ten-year-old records show that “wait for everyone” grew out of a time when arrivals were largely synchronized, while the surrounding discussion in 1 Corinthians 11 about division, eating first, and others going hungry makes “leave six meals in the kitchen” look insufficient. The new practice therefore keeps the scriptural reference while openly acknowledging historical difference and a provisional trial period.

moduleZh.intro: 玛尔塔与托马斯共享同一个目标：不要让晚到的人在共同晚餐中被落下。一个把“彼此等候”落实为全体延后开饭，另一个先提出六点十五分开饭、六份留厨房。十年前记录先削弱了“必须等最后一个人”的历史必然性；随后11章关于分裂、先吃和挨饿的上下文又具体改变了托马斯的方案——从留饭在厨房改成在大厅留席并有人同桌。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 共同体如何把文本、传统处境与当前后果放在一起形成可检验的解释
diagramSteps: 现实处境先让既有实践出现张力

diagramStepNotes: 六点十五分、六点三十五分和七点半构成实际时间压力；两种最初方案都想避免有人被共同用餐落下。
十年前记录显示旧规则产生于多数人六点前已到齐的条件，因此堂区传统仍有意义，却不能直接被当成经文本身规定的钟点。
重读11章不是为了把古代哥林多处境等同现代晚餐，而是让分裂、先吃和挨饿这一文本关系重新进入当前判断。
上下文阅读实际改变了托马斯的流程纸：从“六份留厨房”改为“大厅留六席、保温六份、晚班到后有人同桌”，因此经文并非装饰。
第一次晚餐只覆盖一种到达模式；下一月排班时间更分散，于是小组把试行延长到三个月，并把日期和期限写在卡片背面。
mapping: 正面“彼此等候（林前11:33）”的旧卡片 → 经文以简短提示形式长期参与堂区共同用餐实践，而不是伪装成精确中文直引。
十年前大多数人六点前到齐 → “全员到齐再开饭”曾是特定条件下的合理实践，但不是文本附带的固定时刻。

“六份留厨房”被改成大厅留席并有人同桌 → 文本上下文与当前处境共同改变了具体应用，而不是只做排班折中。
背面日期、6:15安排和三个月试行 → 新做法公开说明依据与边界，也允许后续经验继续检验。
moduleZh.boundary: 神学诠释不等于否定文本确定性，也不等于个人可以任意赋义。不同宗教、教派和解释传统拥有不同经典、权威结构与诠释规范。本故事只呈现一个当代天主教堂区如何把《哥林多前书》11章作为共同晚餐的规范性参照，同时承认古代哥林多聚会与现代堂区周五晚餐并非同一历史和礼仪场景；三个月试行也不是唯一永恒答案，而是一个有公开依据、可继续检验的当前判断。
moduleZh.reflection: 如果门边卡片只是装饰，为什么重读11章之后，托马斯会把原来的“六份留厨房”划掉，改成在大厅留六席并安排有人同桌？

module.intro: Marta and Thomas share the same goal: late arrivals should not be left outside the common meal. One applies “wait for one another” by delaying the whole meal; the other initially proposes beginning at 6:15 and leaving six meals in the kitchen. The ten-year-old records first weaken the idea that waiting for the last person is historically unavoidable. Then the surrounding context in 1 Corinthians 11—division, some eating first, others going hungry—changes Thomas’s proposal in a concrete way: from food held in the kitchen to reserved seats in the hall with someone joining the late arrivals at the table.
module.diagramTitle: How a community brings text, inherited practice, present conditions, and consequences into a testable interpretation
diagramSteps: A present situation creates tension within an inherited practice
The community checks the concrete conditions in which the older practice developed
The scriptural prompt is returned to its wider textual context
Different applications are compared against the community concern they are meant to serve
A provisional practice, time boundary, and method for further testing are recorded publicly
diagramStepNotes: 6:15, 6:35, and 7:30 create a real scheduling pressure, and both initial proposals are trying to keep people from being excluded from the shared meal.

The ten-year-old records show that the earlier rule emerged when most participants had already arrived before 6:00, so the parish tradition still matters but cannot simply be treated as a clock time mandated by the text itself.

Rereading 1 Corinthians 11 is not an attempt to equate ancient Corinth with the modern dinner; it brings the passage’s concern with division, eating first, and others going hungry back into the present judgment.

The contextual reading materially changes Thomas’s workflow note—from “keep six meals in the kitchen” to “reserve six seats in the hall, keep six meals warm, and have someone eat with the late shift”—so the text is not merely decorative.

One dinner covers only one arrival pattern. The next month’s rota has a wider finish window, so the group extends the arrangement to three months and writes both the date and trial period on the back of the card.
mapping: The old card reading “Wait for one another (1 Cor. 11:33)” → Scripture has long functioned as a brief normative prompt within the parish’s common-meal practice rather than as a disguised claim of exact English wording from the whole verse.
Most people arriving before 6:00 ten years earlier → “wait until everyone arrives” was once a reasonable practice under specific conditions, but not a fixed time requirement built into the text.
The discussion of division, eating first, and others going hungry in 1 Corinthians 11 → the isolated prompt is returned to a wider textual relationship.

“Keep six meals in the kitchen” becomes reserved seats in the hall with someone eating alongside the late arrivals → textual context and present circumstances jointly change the concrete application rather than producing a scheduling compromise alone.
The date, 6:15 arrangement, and three-month trial written on the back → the new practice states its basis and boundary publicly while remaining open to further experience and revision.
module.boundary: Theological hermeneutics does not mean denying that texts can have determinate meaning, nor does it mean that individuals may assign any meaning they wish. Different religions, denominations, and interpretive traditions have different canons, authorities, and interpretive norms. This story shows only how one contemporary Catholic parish uses 1 Corinthians 11 as a normative reference for a common meal while acknowledging that an ancient Corinthian gathering and a modern Friday parish dinner are not the same historical or liturgical setting. The three-month trial is not presented as a single eternal answer, but as a present judgment with publicly stated reasons that remains open to further testing.
module.reflection: If the card by the door were only decoration, why would rereading 1 Corinthians 11 lead Thomas to cross out “keep six meals in the kitchen” and replace it with reserved seats in the hall and someone eating with the late arrivals?

articles.title: Delete the Line with “So That”
articles.summary: A handout is almost ready for the printer when the father who submitted the question asks for an explanation of his daughter’s suffering to be removed. The question can stay. What should replace that sentence?
articles.summaryZh: 一张问答卡即将送印，提问的父亲却要求删去女儿受苦的解释。问题可以留下，那句话该怎样改？
storyParagraphs: The print shop would stop accepting orders at 4:30 on Saturday afternoon, and Shen Yao, an editor at a Catholic parish, had to send in a one-page handout for Sunday’s public Q&A before then. The question at the top was already set: “If God is good, knows everything, and has the power to prevent suffering, why does God still permit real suffering?” The question came from Lin Che, whose sixteen-year-old daughter Niannian had been living with chronic pain. Shen Yao’s first version also named the family and added a sentence: “Her pain happened so that the whole parish could learn to care for one another.” Without the family’s approval, the page could not be distributed.

Before 3:00, Lin Che called back. He agreed that the question should stay and wanted it genuinely discussed in the room, but asked Shen Yao to remove Niannian’s name and that explanatory sentence. “People brought meals, drove her places, and helped her keep up with school. All of that is true,” he said. “But that does not tell us why she had to be in pain.” Shen Yao blacked out the name and drew a red circle around the words “so that.” After checking with Niannian, Lin Che called again: the question could be used, he would attend, and Niannian would not.

Once the family’s permission was settled, half the card was still undecided. Shen Yao had planned to insert a full passage from an old handout on human freedom, but after rereading it she kept only a short heading, because it could address some harms caused by human agents but could not directly explain illness. Father Fang, who led the adult catechesis class, came back to collect a book. Together they compressed “stable natural order” into two lines and presented it as one reason that could be discussed, without attaching it to the Lin family’s experience.

At 4:10, Shen Yao laid out the final version. The front still carried the same question. One section listed lines of discussion such as “human freedom” and “a stable natural order”; another stated only that these arguments did not tell readers why Niannian suffered, and that the fact that care had emerged in real life did not prove that the suffering had been arranged in order to produce that care. She sent the PDF to Lin Che. At 4:20 he replied, “You can print it.” Shen Yao immediately sent the file to the print shop.

On Sunday morning, the Q&A gathered around the same handout. One parish member argued that some general reasons at least weakened the claim that God and suffering could never coexist. A neighbor who did not believe in God asked whether severe and apparently unnecessary suffering in the real world still counted as evidence against that belief. Another parent said human freedom did not explain a child’s illness. Father Fang did not merge the three questions into one answer, and Shen Yao wrote the new questions in the blank space on the back of the card.

After the session, Lin Che took one copy of the final version from the entrance table, folded it, and put it in his pocket. Shen Yao filed the first proof back in the folder: the family name was covered in black ink, and the red circle still surrounded the words “so that.” The printer’s trim line remained along the edge of the paper.
storyParagraphsZh: 星期六下午四点半，打印店就停止接单，天主教堂区的编辑沈遥必须在那之前把周日公开问答会的一页卡片送印。最上面的问题已经排好：“如果神是善的、知道一切、也有能力阻止，为什么仍容许真实的苦难？”这句话来自林澈，他十六岁的女儿念念长期受慢性疼痛影响。沈遥第一版还写了林家的名字，并加了一句：“她的痛是为了让整个堂区学会彼此照顾。”没有家属确认，这张纸不能发。
三点前，林澈回了电话。他同意问题继续印，也希望现场真的讨论它，但要删掉念念的名字和那句解释。“大家送饭、接送、陪她补课，这些都是真的，”他说，“可这不能说明她为什么要痛。”沈遥把名字涂黑，又在“为了”两个字外圈了一道红线。林澈问过念念后再次回电：问题可以用，他会到场，念念不来。
家属许可解决后，卡片仍有一半内容没定。沈遥原本想放入一整段关于人的自由的旧讲义，重读后只留下一个短标题，因为它能讨论某些由人造成的伤害，却不能直接解释疾病。负责成人慕道课的方神父回来取书，两人又把“稳定自然秩序”压成两行，写成一种可以讨论的理由，没有把它接到林家的经历后面。
四点十分，沈遥排出最终版：正面仍是那个问题，下面一栏列“人的自由”“稳定自然秩序”等讨论方向；另一栏只标明这些论证没有告诉读者念念为何受苦，也没有因为现实中出现了关爱就证明痛苦为关爱而被安排。她把PDF发给林澈。四点二十分，他回“可以印”。沈遥随即把文件交给打印店。
周日上午，问答会围着同一张卡展开。一位堂区成员认为某些一般理由至少能缓和“神与苦难绝不可能并存”的说法；一位不信神的邻居反问，现实中严重而看似无必要的苦难是否仍构成反对这种信念的证据；另一位家长说，自由意志解释不了孩子的病。方神父没有把三种问题合成一个答案，沈遥把新问题记在卡片背面的空白处。
会后，林澈从入口桌拿了一张最终版，对折放进口袋。沈遥把第一版样张夹回文件夹：林家的名字被黑笔遮住，“为了”两个字外面还留着那道红圈。打印店的裁切线贴在纸边。
explanationParagraphs: Theodicy addresses a classic tension: if God is understood as good, all-powerful, and all-knowing, why do real and serious evil and suffering still exist? A theodicy tries to propose reasons why God actually permits evil or suffering, such as the value of human freedom, soul-making, or a stable natural order. Different proposals compete with one another and face substantial criticism.

This must be distinguished from two other tasks. A logical defence needs only to describe a possible situation in which God’s traditional attributes and the existence of evil are not logically incompatible. The evidential problem of evil instead asks whether the amount, kinds, and distribution of evil in the real world count as evidence against the relevant theistic belief. Both differ from proposing God’s actual reasons for permitting evil, and neither automatically explains why one particular person suffers.
explanationParagraphsZh: 神义论面对一个经典张力：如果神被理解为善、全能并全知，真实而严重的恶与苦难为何仍存在？神义论试图提出神实际容许恶或苦难的理由，例如人的自由、灵魂塑造或稳定自然秩序可能具有的价值。不同方案彼此竞争，也受到重要批评。
这要与另外两类任务区分。逻辑辩护只需提出一种可能情形，说明神的传统属性与恶的存在并非逻辑上必然不相容；针对恶的证据性问题，则考察现实中恶的数量、类型和分布是否构成反对相关有神论信念的证据。二者都不同于提出神实际容许恶的理由，也都不能自动说明某个具体人的苦难为何发生。
articles.overallZh: 这篇讲的是神义论：面对善、全知、全能的神与真实苦难，人们尝试寻找神容许恶的理由。林澈承认大家的照顾，却不愿把照顾说成女儿受苦的目的。讨论一般理由、说明逻辑上可能相容、衡量现实苦难的证据分量，是不同的工作；它们也不能直接给出念念受苦的原因。
articles.overall: This story introduces theodicy: the search for reasons why a good, all-knowing, all-powerful God permits evil and suffering. Lin Che acknowledges the care people gave his daughter but will not call it the purpose of her pain. Proposing general reasons, showing possible logical compatibility, and weighing the evidence of real suffering are different tasks. None directly establishes why Niannian suffers.

moduleZh.intro: 同一张问答卡上，可以提出几种不同的问题：神为什么容许苦难？神与苦难是否可能并存？现实中如此多的苦难是否削弱这种信念？先分清各自在问什么，才能看出一个回答解释了多少，又留下了什么。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 神义论、逻辑辩护与恶的证据性问题分别承担什么任务
diagramSteps: 先面对神的善、能力、知识与真实苦难之间的张力
神义论提出神实际可能容许某类恶的理由
逻辑辩护只需说明神与恶存在一种可能相容的情形
证据性问题继续追问现实恶是否削弱相关信念的可信度
具体个案原因仍需与上述一般论证保持区分
diagramStepNotes: 卡片首先保留林澈的问题：善、全知、全能的神为何仍容许真实苦难？
人的自由与稳定自然秩序是可讨论的一般理由；每一种都有适用范围，也会受到反对。
周日有人只主张神与苦难可能相容；这项主张不必给出神实际容许恶的理由。
邻居追问严重而看似无必要的苦难是否构成反证，即使逻辑相容，证据问题仍然存在。
送饭、接送和补课确实发生了；这些后来的善举仍不能告诉林家，念念为何受苦。
mapping: 卡片顶部始终保留‘善、全知、全能的神为何容许苦难’ → 哲学张力没有被编辑伦理替代。
林澈认可送饭、接送与补课却删掉‘为了’ → 后续善举不能证明苦难的神圣目的。
自由意志段落被缩到一般讨论方向 → 某种神义论理由只在其适用范围内承担解释。
周日有人讨论可能相容、有人提出现实恶的证据性挑战 → 不同哲学任务在事件中保持区分。
第一版红圈与最终版并存 → 可公开讨论一般理由，同时仍不声称知道念念受苦的实际原因。
moduleZh.boundary: 神义论不是证明每一项苦难都有我们能够识别的充分理由，也不是要求反对者接受某一解释。Leibniz 是重要历史来源，但本故事不证明最佳可能世界理论。神义论试图提出实际理由；逻辑辩护只处理可能相容性；证据性问题考察现实恶的证据分量。三者都不能单凭一般论证断言念念为何受苦。 人物与经历均为虚构，场景限于一个当代天主教堂区，不代表所有宗教传统。
moduleZh.reflection: 为什么在林澈已经同意公开问题之后，沈遥仍不能把‘堂区后来更会照顾人’写成念念受苦的理由？

module.intro: The same handout can hold several questions: Why does God permit suffering? Could God and suffering coexist? Does the suffering we actually see weaken that belief? Distinguishing the questions helps us see what an answer explains and what it leaves unresolved.
module.diagramTitle: What different tasks are theodicy, logical defence, and the evidential problem of evil trying to do?
diagramSteps: Begin with the tension between divine goodness, power, knowledge, and real suffering
A theodicy proposes reasons why God might actually permit some kinds of evil
A logical defence needs only to show one possible way in which God and evil could coexist
The evidential problem continues by asking whether real-world evil lowers the credibility of the relevant belief
The actual cause of a particular case remains separate from these general arguments
diagramStepNotes: The handout begins with Lin Che’s question: why does a good, all-knowing, all-powerful God still permit real suffering?
Human freedom and a stable natural order are general reasons that can be discussed. Each has limits and faces objections.
One participant on Sunday argues only that God and suffering could coexist. That claim need not identify God’s actual reason for permitting evil.
The neighbor asks whether severe and apparently unnecessary suffering counts as counterevidence. Logical compatibility leaves that evidential question open.
The meals, rides, and tutoring really happened. Those later acts of care still do not tell the family why Niannian suffers.
mapping: The question at the top always remains “Why would a good, all-knowing, all-powerful God permit suffering?” → the philosophical tension is not replaced by editorial ethics.
Lin Che acknowledges meals, rides, and tutoring but removes “so that” → later good actions cannot prove a divine purpose for the suffering.
The human-freedom passage is reduced to a general line of discussion → one theodical reason carries explanatory weight only within its proper range.
On Sunday, one person discusses possible compatibility while another raises the evidential force of real suffering → distinct philosophical tasks remain separate within the events.
The first proof with its red circle remains beside the final version → general reasons may be discussed publicly without claiming to know the actual reason for Niannian’s suffering.
module.boundary: Theodicy does not prove that every instance of suffering has a sufficient reason that we can identify, nor does it require critics to accept any proposed explanation. Leibniz is an important historical source, but this story does not prove a best-possible-world theory. Theodicy proposes actual reasons; logical defence addresses possible compatibility; the evidential problem assesses the evidential weight of real evil. None of these general arguments alone establishes why Niannian suffers. The characters and experiences are fictional. The setting is one contemporary Catholic parish and does not represent every religious tradition.
module.reflection: Why, even after Lin Che agrees to make the question public, can Shen Yao still not write that “the parish learned to care better” was the reason Niannian suffered?

referencesZh.citation: Leibniz, G. W. (1710). Theodicy: Essays on the Goodness of God, the Freedom of Man and the Origin of Evil. Translated by E. M. Huggard.
referencesZh.use: 作为神义论的经典历史来源，用于说明哲学传统曾系统尝试调和神的善、能力与恶的存在；本故事不宣称由此证明“最佳可能世界”。

referencesZh.citation: Tooley, M. (2025). The Problem of Evil. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, Fall 2025 Edition.
referencesZh.use: 用于支持恶的问题的哲学结构，并区分提出实际理由的神义论、处理逻辑相容性的辩护，以及考察现实恶证据分量的论证任务；这些任务都不自动给出具体个案的实际原因。

references.citation: Leibniz, G. W. (1710). Theodicy: Essays on the Goodness of God, the Freedom of Man and the Origin of Evil. Translated by E. M. Huggard.
references.use: Used as a classic historical source on theodicy, showing how the philosophical tradition has systematically tried to reconcile divine goodness and power with the existence of evil; the story does not claim that this proves a “best possible world.”

references.citation: Tooley, M. (2025). The Problem of Evil. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, Fall 2025 Edition.
references.use: Used to support the philosophical structure of the problem of evil and to distinguish theodicy, which proposes actual reasons, from defences addressing logical compatibility and arguments assessing the evidential weight of real evil; none of these tasks automatically gives the actual reason for a particular case.

articles.title: What Should the Label Say About That Warehouse?
articles.summary: The exhibit label goes to print at four, but Tang Yin has not yet found grounds for the words “temporary clinic.” The layout editor is waiting for her answer.
articles.summaryZh: 下午四点展签就要送印，唐茵还没找到“临时诊所”四个字的依据；排版同事正在等她确认。
storyParagraphs: The River Estuary Town museum is rebuilding its display on the 1951 flood, and the exhibit label has to go to print before 4:00 p.m. An older commemorative booklet described a warehouse photograph as a “temporary clinic during the flood,” and the new label has repeated those words. Tang Yin has one narrow question to resolve: do the available materials support the claim that the inside of the warehouse was used continuously for medical treatment?

She starts by following the footnote on the new label. A recent tourism website cites a 1980 local commemorative booklet, and the booklet’s footnote points to a summary of a 1965 oral-history interview. The wording becomes more confident across the three texts, but the number of sources does not increase: both the website and the booklet depend on the same interview. Tang Yin draws arrows across the three printouts and groups them first as a single transmission chain.

The person interviewed in 1965 recalled people collecting bandages and hot water at the warehouse entrance. The summary says that he had queued outside, but does not record whether he went in. Tang Yin next checks the town council’s 1952 relief-dispatch report. In the supplies column she finds “medical supplies sent to the old warehouse”; a separate personnel column records “a nursing team dispatched to the East River district.” She copies the page number into the margin. Beside it, the words “inside the warehouse” remain.

She divides the worksheet into three columns: “sent to the warehouse,” “collected at the entrance,” and “treatment inside.” The report’s words go into the first column and the interview excerpt into the second. She has nothing to enter in the third. The nursing team is listed only as dispatched to East River, so she keeps that item outside the columns with a note: “location to check.” The layout editor sends the final proof; space for the photograph caption is already reserved beneath “temporary clinic.”

Tang Yin sends back new wording: “A 1952 town council report records medical supplies being sent to the old warehouse; a 1965 oral-history interview recalls people collecting bandages and hot water at its entrance. The available materials do not yet establish whether the interior continuously served as a treatment site.” It is longer than the old heading. Her colleague moves the photograph caption down a line to make room for the last sentence. Tang Yin adds a research lead to the worksheet: an independent source with access to activity inside.

When the print proof goes into the folder, the source diagram goes beside it: the tourism website points to the booklet, and the booklet to the 1965 interview. The 1952 report has one separate box containing its supplies and personnel entries. Before four, her colleague takes the revised label away. Tang Yin files the worksheet. Its third column is still blank, with “activity inside the warehouse” left in the margin for the next search.
storyParagraphsZh: 河口镇展馆要重做1951年洪水展柜，下午四点前必须把展签送印。旧版纪念册把一张仓库照片写成“洪水中的临时诊所”，新展签也照用了这四个字。唐茵只需要解决一个具体问题：现有材料能不能支持“仓库内部曾持续承担诊疗”这句话。
她先追新展签的脚注。近年的旅游网站引用1980年地方纪念册，纪念册脚注又指向1965年的一份口述采访摘要。三段文字的语气越来越肯定，但来源没有增加；网站和纪念册都依赖那份采访。唐茵在三张打印页上画箭头，把它们先归成一条传播链。
1965年的受访者回忆，仓库门口有人领取绷带和热水。摘要写明他当时在门外排队，却没有记下他是否进去过。唐茵接着查1952年的镇议会救灾调拨报告，在物资栏找到“医疗用品送往旧仓库”；人员栏另记“一支护理队被派往河东片区”。她把报告页码抄在纸边，旁边仍留着“仓库内部”几个字。
她在工作表上分出三栏：“送往仓库”“门口领取”“室内诊疗”。报告原文放进第一栏，采访摘句放进第二栏；第三栏仍没有能填进去的文字。护理队只写派往河东，她把那一项留在表外，另注“地点待查”。排版同事发来最后一版样张，临时诊所四个字下面已经留好了照片说明的位置。
唐茵把新文字发回去：“1952年镇议会报告记有医疗用品送往旧仓库；一份1965年的口述采访回忆，有人在仓库门口领取绷带和热水。现有材料尚不足以确认仓库内部是否持续作为诊疗地点。”这段比原来的标题长，同事把照片说明挪下一行，给最后一句留出位置。唐茵在工作表上记下新的待查方向：能见到室内活动的独立材料。
打印样张夹进文件夹时，来源图也放在旁边：旅游网站指向纪念册，纪念册指向1965年采访；1952年报告另占一个框，框内分写物资和人员两项。四点前，同事带走了改过的展签。唐茵把工作表收进档案夹，第三栏还是空的，页边留着下一次要查的“仓库内部活动”。
articles.overall: Source criticism examines who created a source, when and why, what the creator could observe, and whether sources depend on one another. Reliability is assessed against a specific claim; repeated citation is not independent corroboration.
articles.overallZh: 史料批判围绕一个具体历史主张，检查材料由谁、何时、为何留下，作者能看到什么，以及不同材料是否相互依赖。可靠性要按主张判断，重复转引不能当作独立互证。
explanationParagraphs: Source criticism does not begin by sorting material into “official” and “private” and then deciding which is true. It asks who created a source, when, for what purpose and audience, what facts the creator could access, and whether different sources depend on one another.

Reliability must be judged against a specific claim. The report can support “supplies were sent to the warehouse,” and the interview can support a memory of activity at the entrance, but neither alone confirms continuous treatment inside. Lack of confirming evidence also does not prove that nothing happened there.
explanationParagraphsZh: 史料批判不是按“官方/私人”先判真假，而是问谁留下材料、何时形成、用途与受众是什么、作者能接触到哪些事实，以及材料之间是否相互依赖。
可靠性要针对具体主张判断。报告可支持“用品被送往仓库”，采访可支持门口活动记忆，但两者都不足以单独确认仓库内部持续诊疗；缺证也不能反推绝无其事。

module.intro: A historical claim has to be broken down by source identity, scope of access, and whether the materials are genuinely independent.
module.diagramTitle: How “Temporary Clinic” Becomes a Set of Testable Claims
diagramSteps: Identify the exact sentence to be tested
Trace the dependence of later texts on earlier sources
Record exactly what each source says
Compare each source’s scope of access with the claim
Rewrite to match the support and preserve what remains unknown
diagramStepNotes: The question is whether the warehouse interior continuously served a treatment function.
The website → commemorative booklet → 1965 interview forms one dependent chain.
The 1952 report says supplies were sent to the warehouse and the nursing team went to East River; the interview says people collected bandages and hot water at the entrance.
These materials touch supplies, entrance activity, and district-level aid, but do not directly cover continuous treatment inside.
The label states only what the sources support, while the unresolved point stays on the research worksheet.
mapping: Tourism website and commemorative booklet → later transmission materials, not independent corroboration.
1965 interview → supports the interviewee’s remembered scope of activity at the entrance.
1952 town council report → supports supplies being sent to the warehouse and a nursing team being dispatched to the district.
Source diagram → makes the dependency chain and separate materials visible.
module.boundary: A source having a particular purpose or position does not make it automatically false; official records can omit local detail, and private memories can preserve accurate partial observations. The absence of material confirming continuous treatment inside does not prove that no brief aid or treatment ever occurred there.
module.reflection: If several later claims all travel through the same interview, what kind of source with a different scope of access would you need in order to add genuinely independent evidence about activity inside the warehouse?

moduleZh.intro: 同一历史主张要拆开检查来源身份、接触范围和材料独立性。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: “临时诊所”怎样被拆成可核对主张
diagramSteps: 锁定要检验的具体句子
追后期文字的来源依赖
记录每份材料直接说了什么
比较材料与主张的接触范围
按支持范围改写并保留未知
diagramStepNotes: 待检验的是仓库内部是否持续承担诊疗。
网站→纪念册→1965采访是一条依赖链。
1952报告写用品送往仓库、护理队去河东；采访写门口领取绷带和热水。
这些材料触及物资、门口活动和片区救助，但没有直接覆盖室内持续诊疗。
展签只写可支持内容，未确认部分留在工作表。
mapping: 网站与纪念册 → 后期传播材料，不构成独立互证。
1965采访 → 支持受访者对门口活动的记忆范围。
1952议会报告 → 支持用品被送往仓库和护理队派往片区。
来源图 → 显示依赖链与独立材料的位置。
moduleZh.boundary: 材料有特定用途或立场，不等于必然虚假；官方记录可能遗漏现场细节，私人记忆也可能准确保存局部事实。没有材料确认室内持续诊疗，也不能证明仓库内从未发生短暂救助或诊疗。
moduleZh.reflection: 如果几个后来的说法都沿着同一份采访传播，你还需要什么接触范围不同的材料，才能真正增加对仓库内部活动的独立证据？

articles.title: How Should the Five Contexts Be Linked?
articles.summary: The trench will be covered tomorrow. Qian Yu’s relationship diagram is still blank, and the provisional type of one sherd seems at odds with the pit boundary before her.
articles.summaryZh: 探沟第二天就要盖上保护层。钱瑜的关系图还空着，一块陶片的类型判断又与眼前的坑边界对不上。
storyParagraphs: The narrow trench beside an old pottery workshop is due to receive its protective covering the next day. Qian Yu crouches before the cleaned section and takes the numbered cards from her bag: C01 natural yellow soil, C02 dark gray activity layer, C03 pit cut, C04 brown pit fill, and C05 the uppermost pale leveling layer. The sheets for these five recorded units, or contexts, are half filled in, but the relationship diagram is blank. Reopening the trench later will take another arrangement; she wants a complete record of the interfaces she can see clearly today.

The problem comes from a pottery sherd in C04. The finds record provisionally labels it an “earlier type,” and it appears earlier than most fragments from C02. If the artifact alone were used, the pit might also seem early. But when Qian Yu traces the section, the boundary of C03 clearly cuts into C02. The cut is identified first from the visible change in soil color and texture, not inferred backward from the pottery date.

Qian Yu records the C03 cut and the C04 fill separately. C03 must be later than the C02 layer it cuts, and C04 can only have entered the pit after the cut existed. The apparently earlier sherd only suggests that the object itself may be earlier. It may be residual material or may have been redeposited into the fill later; the exposed interfaces do not show exactly how it entered C04.

Above them, C05 continuously covers C04 and the surviving C02 beside the pit. On the context sheet Qian Yu enters both “overlies C04” and “overlies C02.” Beside it she draws a sequence from earlier to later: C01 → C02 → C03 → C04 → C05. She makes the four arrows clear, then returns to the section drawing and adds the stretch of boundary where the pale soil continues over the gray layer outside the pit.

The scale in the photograph runs beside the pit edge. Qian Yu compares it with the section drawing, checking where C02 overlies C01, C03 cuts into C02, and C04 fills C03. The sherd remains linked to the C04 finds-bag number, while its type assessment stays in a separate finds record. No year is entered in the box for the pit’s date, but the relationship field now says “later than C02.”

Before work stops, all five context numbers are entered on the section drawing, with C03 marked as a cut and C04 as a fill. The relationship sheet is filed behind the photograph list, and the simplified four-arrow sequence sits on the facing page. The pottery bag still bears C04. The last photograph before the protective covering is placed shows the five context numbers and the clearly visible pit boundary.
storyParagraphsZh: 旧陶作坊院墙旁的窄探沟，第二天就要铺上保护层。钱瑜蹲在清理好的剖面前，把编号卡从袋里拿出来：C01自然黄土，C02深灰活动层，C03坑的切口，C04坑内褐色填土，C05最上面的浅色整平层。五个层位单元的表格已经填了一半，关系图却还空着。覆盖以后若要复查，得再安排开放；今天能直接看清的界面，她想先记录完整。
问题来自C04里的一块陶片。器物记录暂写“较早类型”，看起来比C02里多数碎片更早。如果只看器物，坑似乎也该很早；但剖面上的C03边界清楚切进C02，切口轮廓先由土色和质地界面识别出来，并不是根据陶片年代倒推出来。
钱瑜把C03切口和C04填土分开记录。C03必须晚于它切穿的C02；C04又是在切口形成后才进入坑内。那块较早类型陶片只说明器物本身可能更早，它可能是残留物或后来再沉积进填土，具体怎样进入C04，当前界面并不能确定。
再往上，C05连续盖住C04，也覆盖坑边仍保存的C02。钱瑜在层位单元表上分别填下“覆盖C04”“覆盖C02”。旁边另画一条从早到晚的顺序：C01→C02→C03→C04→C05。她把四支箭头描清，回到剖面图上，又补上浅色土一直延到坑外灰层的那段边线。
照片上的比例尺刚好横在坑边，钱瑜拿它对照剖面图，再核一遍C02覆盖C01、C03切进C02、C04填进C03的位置。陶片仍挂在C04的器物袋编号下，类型判断写在单独的器物记录里。挖坑日期那一格没有填写年份，关系栏里却已经有了“晚于C02”。
收工前，五个context编号都写进剖面图，C03标为cut，C04标为fill。关系表夹在照片单后面，简化的四箭头顺序图放在旁页；陶片袋仍贴着C04。加保护层前最后一张照片拍的是这五个编号和清楚的坑边界。
articles.overall: Stratigraphy uses relationships of superposition, cutting, and filling to establish relative event order. An artifact can be made, used, and deposited at different times, so its type cannot replace the sequence supported by soil interfaces.
articles.overallZh: 地层学利用覆盖、切穿和填入关系建立相对事件顺序。器物的制造、使用和沉积可能发生在不同时间，器物类型不能替代土层界面所支持的先后关系。
explanationParagraphs: In an undisturbed sequence, lower deposits are generally earlier, but cuts disrupt simple depth order. Relative order depends on what overlies what, what cuts through what, and what fills the cut. A cut and its fill are separate contexts and must be numbered and recorded separately.

The manufacture or use date of an artifact is not the same as its deposition date. An apparently earlier sherd can appear as residual or redeposited material in a later fill; without independent dating evidence, stratigraphic relationships mainly support relative sequence.
explanationParagraphsZh: 未扰动序列中，下层通常较早；切口会破坏简单深度顺序。相对先后要看谁覆盖谁、谁切穿谁、什么填入切口。切口与填土是不同层位单元，须分别编号记录。
器物制造或使用时间不等于沉积时间。较早类型陶片可作为残留或再沉积物出现在较晚填土；没有独立年代证据时，地层关系主要支持相对先后。

module.intro: Stratigraphic recording begins with visible interfaces and converts direct relationships among layers, cuts, and fills into a relative event sequence.
module.diagramTitle: The Minimum Relative Sequence from C01 to C05
diagramSteps: C01 natural yellow soil exists first
C02 dark gray layer overlies C01
C03 pit cuts through C02
C04 brown fill enters C03
C05 pale layer overlies C04 and surviving C02
diagramStepNotes: C01 is the basal recorded unit, or context, in this trench.
C02 has a direct superposition relationship with C01.
C03 records the cut left by digging the pit, rather than a soil layer; it is later than the C02 it cuts.
C04 is the pit fill and is later than the cut; the apparently earlier sherd may be residual or redeposited material.
C05 directly covers C04 and also the surviving C02 outside the pit.
mapping: C03 cuts C02 → digging the pit is later than the dark gray layer.
C04 fills C03 → backfilling is later than digging the pit.
C05 covers C04 and surviving C02 → leveling belongs to a later event.
Apparently early sherd in C04 → artifact dating evidence must be separated from deposition dating.
module.boundary: “Lower is earlier” applies only to undisturbed relationships. Cuts, fills, redeposition, and missing deposits disrupt simple depth order. The four-arrow side diagram is only a simplified event chain, not a complete Harris Matrix; absolute dates also cannot be inferred without independent chronological evidence.
module.reflection: An apparently earlier sherd lies in the fill of a pit cutting a previously deposited layer. Which interfaces support the sequence of digging and filling, and which artifact details remain dating clues to be checked?

moduleZh.intro: 地层记录从可见界面出发，把层、切口和填土之间的直接关系转换成相对事件顺序。
diagramSteps: C01自然黄土先存在
C02深灰层覆盖C01
C03坑切穿C02
C04褐色填土进入C03
C05浅色层覆盖C04与残存C02
diagramStepNotes: C01是本探沟记录中的基底层位单元。
C02与C01有直接覆盖关系。
C03记录挖坑留下的切口，不是一层土；它晚于被切的C02。
C04是坑填土，晚于切口形成；较早类型陶片可能是残留或再沉积物。
C05直接盖住C04，也盖住坑外残存C02。
mapping: C03切C02 → 挖坑晚于深灰层。
C04填C03 → 回填晚于挖坑。
C05盖C04与残存C02 → 整平属于更晚事件。
较早类型陶片在C04 → 器物年代线索与沉积年代需分开。
moduleZh.boundary: “下层较早”只适用于未被扰动的关系。切口、回填、再沉积和缺失层会破坏简单深度顺序。四箭头旁图只是简化事件链，不等于完整Harris Matrix；没有独立年代证据时也不能推出绝对年份。
moduleZh.reflection: 一块较早类型陶片出现在切穿已有土层的坑填土中。哪些界面支持挖坑与回填的先后，哪些器物信息仍只能作为待核查的年代线索？

references.citation: Harris, E. C. (1989). Principles of Archaeological Stratigraphy (2nd ed.). Academic Press.
references.use: Supports systematic representation of archaeological stratigraphic sequence and the Harris Matrix; the bibliographic source is not used to claim that stratigraphy was first invented by a single author.

references.citation: Historic England (2018). Excavation Recording Manual, Modules 2–3.
references.use: Supports recording methods for cuts, fills, stratigraphic relationships, and archaeological field contexts.

referencesZh.use: 支持考古层序与Harris Matrix的系统化表达；书目来源不用于宣称地层学由单一作者首次发明。

articles.title: The Green Door in the Side Alley
articles.summary: The old bicycle shop needs an accessible entrance. In a metal box, the owner’s daughter finds two original plans. How did the familiar green door become the one everyone uses?
articles.summaryZh: 老自行车店要改入口，女儿从铁盒里翻出两份旧图。今天熟悉的绿门，当年是怎么留下来的？
storyParagraphs: By Friday, Lin Cheng had to submit an accessibility renovation plan for her father’s old bicycle shop to the landlord. Customers now entered through the green door in the side alley, but the threshold was too high, so she was planning a ramp and an automatic door. The architect asked whether they should also reopen the old doorway onto the main street. Lin Cheng immediately shook her head. “That wall has always been shelving.” Only after she went home did she realize that the shop had been open for more than thirty years and she had never asked why customers had not used the street entrance on the first day.

After closing that evening, she opened an old metal document box. Inside were two floor plans from the year the shop opened, both signed by the landlord as “approved for construction.” The matching carpenter’s quotations also listed prices and schedules, with little difference between them. Plan A opened onto the main street with the counter farther back; Plan B used the existing side-alley doorway. Between them sat a roadworks notice stating that the main-street pavement would be opened for utility work starting one week before the planned opening and would remain under construction for six weeks, with only residential access maintained. The side alley was unaffected.

Cash-ledger pages in the same box made the timing even tighter: the first shipment of complete bicycles was already scheduled to arrive in the second week of the works, and the first full month’s rent also began that week. Beside Plan B, her father had written, “Open through the alley first; reconsider when the street is restored.” The roadworks ended six weeks later. The next day, a carpenter’s remeasurement sheet recorded the street doorway dimensions and a three-day construction schedule. Only two days after that did her father sign the order for a full wall of bicycle racks, which was installed the following week.

The later records kept changing. After the racks were installed, the repair bench moved from the back wall to a position closer to the side door. Over the next few months, delivery notes gradually changed their instruction to “enter through alley.” Lin Cheng copied the dates in sequence along the edge of the renovation plan and then showed them to her father. He added only one detail: building the front-door option had presented no technical difficulty; they used the alley first because the shop had to open on time, and every later change meant that switching back to the street would require moving a little more.

On Thursday, Lin Cheng and the architect measured both entrances again. The old street doorway could still be restored, but now it would require removing about one-third of the bicycle racks, moving the checkout counter, and reorganizing access to the repair bench. The alley option mainly required lowering the threshold and moving one display unit. She drew both options into the new plan and finally circled the side alley because it required less disruption in the present layout and still worked well for rolling complete bicycles in and out.

Before submitting the application, Lin Cheng copied the original approved A and B plans, both quotations, the six-week roadworks notice, and the new measurements for both current options, and stapled them behind the landlord’s form. The originals went back into the metal box. At closing time, her father pulled the green door shut; behind the wall facing the main street, the earliest row of bicycle racks was still in place.
storyParagraphsZh: 星期五前，林澄得把父亲那间老自行车店的无障碍改造图交给房东。顾客现在都从侧巷那扇绿门进出，门槛太高，她准备做缓坡和自动门。建筑师问要不要顺便恢复朝大街的旧门洞，林澄马上摇头：“那面墙一直都是货架。”回家后她才想起，店开了三十多年，自己从没问过第一天为什么不是从大街进。
晚上收店后，她翻出一只铁皮文件盒。里面有开店那年的两张平面草图，房东在A、B两张上都签了“可施工”；对应的木工报价也都写明价格和工期，差距不大。A方案在大街开门、柜台靠后，B方案使用侧巷已有门洞。夹在中间的施工通知却写着，大街人行道将在开业前一周开始连续六周铺管，店面只能保留住户通行，侧巷不受影响。
同一盒里的现金账页又把时间卡得更紧：首批整车已经约在施工开始后的第二周到店，第一笔完整月租也从那周起算。父亲在B方案旁写了“先从巷口开，路面恢复再看”。道路工程六周后结束。第二天，一张木工复量单又记录了大街门洞尺寸和三天工期；两天后，父亲才签下整面挂车架的订单，货架在下一周安装完成。
后面的记录继续变了。货架装好后，维修台从后墙移到靠侧门的位置；几个月内，送货单的备注也逐渐改成“巷口进”。林澄把这些日期按顺序抄到改造图边上，再拿给父亲核对。父亲只补了一句：当年做前门没有技术难处，先走侧巷是为了按时开门，后来每改一处，换回前街就要多动一些东西。
周四，林澄和建筑师重新量了两处入口。大街旧门洞仍可恢复，但现在要拆掉约三分之一挂车架、移动收银台，并重新安排维修台的进出；侧巷方案主要是降低门槛、调整一组展示架。她把两种方案都画进新图，最后圈了侧巷，因为在今天的布局里改动更少，也仍方便整车进出。
提交申请前，林澄把当年的A、B获批草图、两份报价、六周施工通知和新的两方案测量图各复印一份，订在房东表格后面。原件重新放回铁盒。关店时，父亲把绿门拉上；大街那面墙后，最早的一排挂车架还在原位。
explanationParagraphs: Historical contingency emphasizes that later outcomes often depend on particular conditions, feasible choices, and the order in which events occurred; from the starting point, there was not necessarily only one inevitable path. Recognizing contingency does not deny causes, structural constraints, or human skill. On the contrary, analysis must show which options genuinely existed at the time, which conditions changed the choice, and how later events made one path increasingly stable.

Research on path dependence is adjacent to this question: earlier choices can alter later costs, resource allocation, and the range of available action, making it harder to return to another option. But historical contingency is not the same thing as path dependence, and neither is it pure luck. Serious claims that “things could have gone differently” are strongest when contemporaneous plans, approvals, quotations, records, or actions show that the alternative genuinely existed.
explanationParagraphsZh: 历史偶然性强调，后来形成的结果往往依赖当时具体条件、可行选择与事件先后顺序，并不是从起点看就只有一条必然道路。承认偶然性并不等于否认原因、结构约束或人的能力；分析反而需要说明当时哪些选项真实存在、哪些条件改变了选择，以及后续事件怎样让某条路径变得更稳固。
路径依赖研究与这一问题相邻：较早的选择可能改变后续成本、资源配置与行动范围，使回到另一方案越来越困难。但历史偶然性不等于路径依赖，也不等于纯运气。要认真讨论“本可以不同”，最好有同期计划、批准、报价、记录或行动证明备选曾真实存在。
articles.overallZh: 这篇讲的是历史偶然性。两份获批旧图说明，店铺原本有不止一种可行入口。施工与开业时间让侧门先被采用，后来货架、维修台和送货习惯又改变了改门的成本。今天保留绿门有充分理由，却不能据此认定，当初也只有这一条路。
articles.overall: This story introduces historical contingency. The two approved plans show that the shop originally had more than one workable entrance. Roadworks and opening deadlines led to the alley door being used first; later racks, the repair bench, and delivery habits changed the cost of switching. Keeping the green door makes sense today, but that does not mean it was the only possible path at the beginning.

moduleZh.intro: 铁盒里的文件把同一个入口拆成几个不同时刻：当初能选什么，为什么先这样做，后来又添了哪些改动。按时间读这些记录，才能分清开店时的条件和今天的理由。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 如何用同期证据判断一个结果并非起初唯一必然
diagramSteps: 确认当时存在不止一个可实施的方案
识别具体条件为何让其中一条方案先被采用
检查条件变化后另一方案是否仍被真实考虑
追踪后续投资与组织怎样改变转换成本
把今天的合理选择与当初的必然性分开判断
diagramStepNotes: A、B草图都获房东同意，木工报价和工期相近，说明大街方案不是只有纸上想象。
六周道路工程本身不足以说明选择，还与整车到货和月租开始共同构成不能等待六周的时间压力。
道路恢复第二天重新测量大街门洞，且记录三天施工期，说明前门在临时侧门使用后仍是可执行备选。
整墙货架在前门复量之后下单，下一周安装；随后维修台和送货方式继续围绕侧门调整，改回前门需要搬动的东西逐渐增加。
今天仍选侧门来自现存布局、改造范围和整车动线，不表示当初两种方案概率相同，也不表示侧门从一开始就必然最好。
mapping: 同期获批A、B草图与两份报价 → 两个入口当时都具备实际可施工性。
六周道路施工、租金开始和首批车辆到店 → 结构条件与资源时间共同推动侧门先被采用。
道路恢复后的前门复量单 → 临时选择尚未立即变成不可逆结果。
复量后才订货架、随后移动维修台和改变送货路线 → 先后顺序逐渐改变未来转换成本。
今天实测后仍圈侧巷 → 历史结果可依赖偶然条件，同时现阶段继续保留仍有理性原因。
moduleZh.boundary: 历史偶然性不等于历史没有原因，也不等于所有备选机会相同。技能、资金、时间、空间和制度条件都会限制行动。路径依赖可解释早期选择如何影响后续成本，但它只是相邻机制，不能替代对当时备选与先行条件的历史证明。这个店铺及其全部档案均为虚构，不冒充真实地方史。
moduleZh.reflection: 今天保留绿门的理由，哪些是开店时已有的，哪些是后来才出现的？

module.intro: The documents in the metal box let us follow the same entrance through different moments: what could be chosen at first, why one option came first, and what changed afterward. Reading the records in order separates the conditions at opening from the reasons for today’s choice.
module.diagramTitle: How contemporaneous evidence can show that an outcome was not the only inevitable path from the start
diagramSteps: Confirm that more than one option was actually feasible at the time
Identify the concrete conditions that made one option come first
Check whether the alternative was still seriously considered after those conditions changed
Trace how later investment and organization changed the cost of switching
Separate the reasonableness of today’s choice from claims of inevitability at the beginning
diagramStepNotes: Both A and B plans were approved by the landlord, and the carpenter’s quotations and schedules were similar, showing that the street option was more than a paper fantasy.
The six-week roadworks alone do not explain the choice; the first bicycle shipment and the start of full rent together create the time pressure that made waiting six weeks costly.

The main-street doorway was remeasured the day after the works ended, with a three-day construction schedule recorded, showing that the front entrance remained an executable option after temporary use of the alley.

The racks were ordered after the street doorway was remeasured and installed the following week. Later changes to the repair bench and deliveries left more things to move if the street entrance was restored.

Choosing the alley again today reflects the current layout, renovation scope, and bicycle flow. It does not imply that the original options had equal probability or that the alley was inevitably best from the outset.
mapping: Contemporaneous approved A and B plans plus two quotations → both entrances were genuinely buildable at the time.
Six weeks of street works, the start of rent, and the first bicycle delivery → structural conditions and resource timing jointly pushed the alley option to be used first.
The front-door remeasurement after the street reopened → the temporary choice had not yet become irreversible.
The rack order came after remeasurement, followed later by the repair-bench move and changing delivery route → event sequence gradually changed the future cost of switching.
Today’s measurement still leads Lin Cheng to circle the alley → an outcome can depend on contingent historical conditions while still having rational reasons for being retained now.
module.boundary: Historical contingency does not mean that history has no causes or that all alternatives were equally likely. Skill, money, time, space, and institutional conditions constrain action. Path dependence can help explain how early choices alter later costs, but it is an adjacent mechanism and cannot replace historical evidence that the alternative genuinely existed at the time. The shop and all of its records in this story are fictional and do not claim to be real local history.
module.reflection: Which reasons for keeping the green door today already existed when the shop opened, and which developed later?

referencesZh.citation: Sewell, W. H., Jr. (2005). Logics of History: Social Theory and Social Transformation. University of Chicago Press.
referencesZh.use: 用于支持把历史结果放在具体历史时间、事件、结构条件和行动者选择之间理解；不把 Sewell 表述为“历史偶然性”概念的唯一首创者。

references.use: Used to support understanding historical outcomes through the relations among historical time, events, structural conditions, and actors’ choices; Sewell is not presented as the sole originator of the idea of historical contingency.

articles.title: Should the Blue Card Stay?
articles.summary: Before an exhibition opens, a conservator must decide whether to leave a visitor’s handwritten blue card in place. Old photographs change her understanding, but they do not make the decision for her.
articles.summaryZh: 展览开幕前，保育员要决定一张观众写过的蓝卡是否留下。旧照片改了她的想法，却没有替她作决定。
storyParagraphs: The exhibition was due to open at 6:00, and conservator Mei Lin had one hour left to inspect a newly acquired 1998 installation. The work consisted of a metal frame, thin cords, and a row of removable paper cards. During the internal preview the previous day, an invited community participant had written “For tomorrow’s person” on a blue card and clipped it back onto the cord. Mei Lin wrote in the condition checklist: “Remove blue card before opening.” Her reason was that the museum’s first public presentation of a newly acquired work should begin from a clearly documented baseline state, rather than allowing yesterday’s change to quietly become the institution’s default idea of the work’s original condition.

She opened the first-exhibition archive to check that judgment. In photographs from the first day, most of the cards were blank; two weeks later, many carried handwriting, and later photographs showed cards being replenished and replaced. The old installation note only said that visitors could write on the supplied cards; it did not say that “participation before a formal opening is always invalid.” Mei Lin then found the invitation email for the previous day’s preview: the room had not contained only staff. Several community members had explicitly been invited “as the first users to test the interaction.” Her factual assumption that the entire internal preview was merely backstage activity began to weaken.

But another concern did not disappear. Mei Lin had long held that a museum should not elevate one visitor message into a permanent original simply because it happened to be moving; otherwise there would be no consistent reason for deciding what to do with the next card or the next ten. The curator raised a competing concern: if the museum erased every valid act of participation in order to achieve a visually clean opening image, it could manufacture a “zero-trace starting point” that the work itself had never required.

Mei Lin changed the checklist: the blue card would not be removed before 6:00, because it had been made using the work’s own card and clip by someone invited to participate in the interaction. But she also withdrew another impulse that had just occurred to her—to archive it permanently as “the museum’s first participation card.” Beside the entry, she wrote: “Documenting an opening baseline does not require erasing participation that has already been authorized; valid participation also does not automatically acquire permanent preservation status.” The blue card would remain on the cord with the other written cards for this display cycle.

At 5:40, twenty minutes before opening, an education colleague asked whether a card written by a staff member’s relative during the preview should count in the same way. Mei Lin did not turn every future case into a new rule on the spot. Instead, she added a note: future decisions should consider whether the person had been invited as a user of the interaction or had simply left a trace while present backstage; if the evidence was unclear, the museum should document the case rather than immediately make it permanent. She added the invitation email’s reference number to the conservation note and recorded that on Monday the curatorial and education teams would decide on a consistent rotation or selective-archiving standard for that week’s cards.

At 6:00, the first visitors entered. Someone took a white card from the box, wrote on it, and clipped it beside the blue one. By closing time, several more new cards hung beside it. Mei Lin photographed the entire cord as a record and entered the camera reference number on the checklist. The blue card was still held by its original clip; it had not been placed on its own in a permanent archive folder.
storyParagraphsZh: 下午六点展览开幕，保育员梅琳还有一小时检查新购入的一件1998年装置。作品由金属框、细绳和一排可取下的纸卡组成。前一天内部预览时，一位社区受邀来宾在蓝卡上写了“给明天的人”，又夹回绳上。梅琳先在检查表写下“开幕前移除蓝卡”：她认为新购藏作品第一次正式开放时，应从记录清楚的基准状态开始，不能让昨天的变化悄悄变成馆方默认的原作状态。
她翻首展档案核对这个判断。第一天照片里大多数卡片空白，两周后的照片却已有许多字迹；后续照片又显示纸卡会被补充、更换。旧安装说明只说观众可以在提供的卡片上书写，并没有规定“正式开幕前的参与一律无效”。梅琳又找到昨天预览的邀请邮件：来的不只是工作人员，几位社区成员被明确邀请来“作为首批使用者测试互动方式”。她原先把整个内部预览都当成后台的想法开始松动。
但另一项考虑没有消失。梅琳一直坚持，博物馆不该因为某一张观众留言特别动人，就擅自把它升级成永久原件；否则下一张、下十张该怎样处理都没有一致理由。策展人则提醒她，若为了得到一个干净的开幕画面而删掉所有有效参与，也会人为制造一种作品从未要求的“零痕迹起点”。
梅琳改了检查表：蓝卡不在六点前移除，因为它确实通过作品提供的卡片和夹子，由被邀请参与互动的人留下。但她也收回了刚冒出来的另一个念头——把它作为“本馆第一张参与卡”永久归档。她在旁边写下：“记录开幕基准，不等于清除已经发生的授权参与；有效参与也不自动获得永久保存资格。”蓝卡先与本轮其他书写卡一起留在绳上。
开幕前二十分钟，教育同事问，那工作人员家属在预览里写的卡算不算同一类。梅琳没有当场把所有未来情况写成规则，只在备注里补了一句：以后要看参与者是作为互动使用者被邀请，还是只在后台工作过程中留下痕迹；若证据不清，就先记录而不是直接永久化。她把昨天的邀请邮件编号写进保育备注，又注明周一要和策展、教育团队一起决定本周卡片采用怎样一致的轮换或抽存标准。
六点开门后，第一批观众进场。有人取出白卡写字，夹到蓝卡旁边。闭馆时，蓝卡旁已经多了几张新卡。梅琳拍了一张整条绳的记录照，把相机编号写进检查表；蓝卡仍留在原来的夹子上，没有被单独装进永久档案袋。
explanationParagraphs: Reflective equilibrium is a method of moving back and forth among considered judgments about particular cases, general principles, and relevant background beliefs, testing and revising them against one another. When conflict appears, the method does not assume that the initial intuition must be right, nor does it merely add exceptions to a rule. Particular judgments, principles, and the factual or theoretical beliefs that support them may all be revised in the search for a more justified overall coherence.

Wide reflective equilibrium also brings alternative principles and relevant background theories into the comparison, rather than seeking harmony only within one existing set of beliefs. Even when a temporary equilibrium is reached, coherence does not guarantee truth; new evidence, objections, or better background theories may reopen the process.
explanationParagraphsZh: 反思平衡是一种在审慎的个案判断、一般原则与相关背景信念之间往返检验和修订的方法。冲突出现时，并不是默认最初直觉必然正确，也不是只给规则不断增加例外；具体判断、原则，以及支撑它们的事实或理论背景都可能被修改，以寻求更有理由的整体融贯。
较宽的反思平衡还要求把替代原则和相关背景理论纳入比较，而不是只在一套既有信念内部求和谐。即使暂时达到融贯，也不能保证结论就是真理；新的证据、反对意见或更好的理论仍可能重新打开调整过程。
articles.overallZh: 这篇讲的是反思平衡。梅琳既重新判断蓝卡，也检查支撑判断的原则和事实：什么算有效参与，怎样记录开幕状态，哪些东西值得永久保存。她允许蓝卡暂留，又用同一套修订后的原则约束自己的珍藏冲动。这种来回检验可以让判断更有理由，但不保证它永远正确。
articles.overall: This story introduces reflective equilibrium. Mei Lin reconsiders the blue card along with the principles and facts behind her judgment: what counts as valid participation, how to document an opening, and what deserves permanent preservation. She leaves the card in place for now while using the revised principles to restrain her own wish to treasure it. This back-and-forth testing can make a judgment better justified without making it correct forever.

moduleZh.intro: 旧照片告诉梅琳纸卡曾经怎样使用，邀请邮件告诉她昨天的来宾为何到场。接下来仍要作判断：留下蓝卡、记录开幕、永久收藏，是否可以同时用一套有理由的原则说明？
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 反思平衡如何让个案、原则与背景信念相互修订
diagramSteps: 先形成一个有理由的个案判断与一般原则
新事实改变支撑原判断的部分背景信念
把相互竞争的原则放到同一具体个案中比较
同时修订个案判断、一般原则和背景理解
用修订后的原则约束新的偏好，并保持后续开放
diagramStepNotes: “开幕前移除蓝卡”来自保护新购藏作品基准状态的审慎考虑，并非随意直觉。
首展照片、安装说明和预览邀请邮件只改变‘参与是否发生、预览是否全属后台’等事实背景，没有直接规定今天应如何处理蓝卡。
“开幕应有可记录基准”与“馆方不应为整洁而抹除有效参与”都是可辩护原则，因此冲突不能靠给旧规则加一个私人例外解决。
梅琳把蓝卡从‘移除’改为‘本轮暂留’，把原则改成‘记录基准不等于清除授权参与’，并修订‘内部预览必然只是后台’这一背景信念。
她随后放弃把蓝卡永久保存为‘第一张’的冲动，因为‘有效参与不自动获得永久资格’这一修订原则也必须约束她自己的偏好；周一的统一标准仍可被新证据修订。
mapping: 最初决定六点前移除蓝卡 → 一个认真形成但可修订的个案判断。
‘正式开放应从记录清楚的基准开始’ → 起初合理的一般保育原则。
预览邀请把部分社区成员列为互动使用者 → 改变‘内部预览全部是后台’的背景信念。
蓝卡暂留但不永久归档 → 个案判断改变，同时两个原则被重新组合而非单向迁就。
放弃‘第一张就永久保存’并留待周一制定一致标准 → 修订后的原则反过来限制人物新产生的偏好，结论仍开放。
moduleZh.boundary: 反思平衡不等于有反思就算，也不等于把几种直觉折中平均。个案判断、一般原则和背景信念都必须能接受彼此以及相关证据的修订；较宽的形式还会比较替代原则和背景理论。即使一组信念暂时更加融贯，也仍可能共同出错，融贯本身不保证真理，新证据与反对意见可以重新打开过程。 人物、1998年装置与档案均为虚构；这是伦理判断的日常类比，不能据此概括全部博物馆保育规范。
moduleZh.reflection: 为什么梅琳在改变‘蓝卡应移除’这个判断之后，又必须放弃把它永久保存为‘第一张参与卡’的想法？

module.intro: The old photographs show Mei Lin how the cards were used, and the invitation explains why yesterday’s visitors were there. She still has to judge whether leaving the blue card, documenting the opening, and deciding what to archive can be explained by a consistent set of justified principles.
module.diagramTitle: How reflective equilibrium revises case judgments, principles, and background beliefs together
diagramSteps: Begin with a reasoned case judgment and a general principle
New facts revise part of the background belief supporting that judgment
Compare competing principles within the same concrete case
Revise the case judgment, the principle, and part of the background understanding together
Use the revised principle to constrain a new preference while keeping the conclusion open
diagramStepNotes: “Remove the blue card before opening” comes from a serious concern about preserving a documented baseline for a newly acquired work, not from an arbitrary intuition.

The exhibition photographs, installation note, and preview invitation change factual beliefs about whether participation occurred and whether the whole preview was merely backstage activity; they do not directly prescribe what should happen to the blue card today.

“The public opening should have a recordable baseline” and “the museum should not erase valid participation merely for visual neatness” are both defensible principles, so the conflict cannot be solved by giving the old rule one private exception.

Mei Lin changes the blue card from “remove” to “leave for this display cycle,” revises the general principle to say that documenting a baseline does not require erasing authorized participation, and revises the background belief that an internal preview is necessarily just backstage activity.

She then gives up the impulse to archive the blue card permanently as “the first one,” because the revised principle that valid participation does not automatically receive permanent status must also constrain her own new preference. Monday’s common standard remains open to further evidence.
mapping: The initial decision to remove the blue card before 6:00 → a seriously formed but revisable judgment about one case.
“A formal opening should begin from a clearly documented baseline” → the initially reasonable general conservation principle.
The preview invitation identifies some community members as users of the interaction → the background belief that the whole internal preview was backstage activity is revised.
The blue card remains but is not permanently archived → the case judgment changes while the two principles are recombined rather than one simply yielding.
Mei Lin gives up permanent preservation of “the first one” and waits until Monday for a consistent standard → the revised principle constrains her new preference and the conclusion remains open.
module.boundary: Reflective equilibrium is not simply any act of reflection, nor is it an averaging of several intuitions. Case judgments, general principles, and background beliefs must all be open to revision in light of one another and relevant evidence; wider forms also compare alternative principles and background theories. Even if a set of beliefs becomes more coherent, they may still be jointly wrong. Coherence itself does not guarantee truth, and new evidence or objections can reopen the process. The characters, 1998 installation, and archives are fictional. This everyday analogy for ethical judgment does not establish general museum conservation standards.
module.reflection: Why, after changing her judgment that the blue card should be removed, does Mei Lin also have to give up the idea of permanently preserving it as “the first participation card”?

articles.title: The Third Strap Was Never Used
articles.summary: During teardown at a community science fair, two carts cross the same threshold together, but only one load damages the borrowed projector. The repair work finds an owner, and so does a new story about who can be trusted.
articles.summaryZh: 社区科学展撤场时，两辆手推车同时经过门槛，只有一边的展板撞坏了借来的投影仪。维修有了归属，关于‘谁更可靠’的说法也随之分开。
storyParagraphs: At 9:00 p.m., the community science fair had half an hour left for teardown, and the borrowed projector had to be returned to the youth center the next morning. Volunteers Ye Lin and Gao Yu each loaded an identical handcart with six folding display panels of similar weight and prepared to push them side by side through the hall’s double doors into storage. The teardown checklist said, “Two straps on level ground; a third strap recommended over uneven surfaces.” Each tightened two straps, shook the outermost panel to check it, and neither went to fetch the third strap hanging on the wall.

A facilities volunteer held both doors open at the same time and directed each cart straight through the door directly in front of it so neither would need to turn suddenly and risk colliding. The metal threshold covers on both sides looked flat, and people had been crossing them all day. Ye Lin’s left wheel rolled over with only a jolt. Almost simultaneously, Gao Yu’s right front wheel pressed onto the other cover; one corner suddenly lifted and knocked the wheel sideways. All six panels leaned to the right, and the outermost one slipped from under the strap and struck the projector case waiting by the door for return.

The facilities volunteer first closed off the right-hand doorway, then lifted the threshold cover. One fastener underneath had come loose; nothing on the surface showed it, and an empty cart passing over had not made the cover lift. Only when a loaded wheel pressed near the edge did the cover rise. Gao Yu steadied the panels, then photographed the scene with the facilities volunteer and recorded the equipment number. The projector housing was cracked and the lens mount bent, so the youth center had to use a backup unit for the class scheduled the next day.

The following day, Gao Yu took the projector to the repair shop under the incident record, while the event organizer filed the repair through its event insurance; the borrowing contract remained the organizer’s responsibility. Over the next few days, the youth center often contacted Gao Yu directly for updates because he had the equipment details and accident photos. At the same time, someone planning the next event asked Ye Lin first whether she could handle valuable equipment again, while people in the group chat began referring to Gao Yu as “the one who broke the projector that time.”

Ye Lin did not decide the issue for anyone. She posted the teardown photo showing both carts: each had only two straps. The facilities volunteer then added photos of the opened threshold cover and the repair record. On the next duty roster, Ye Lin was still assigned to equipment moving, while Gao Yu had been shifted to general setup. Gao Yu still went to collect the repaired projector because he had already arranged the pickup time with the repair company.

A week later, the youth center signed for the projector. Gao Yu returned the repair receipt to the borrowing folder, where the organizer’s insurance papers were still clipped inside. The two carts for the next event were already parked against the wall, and the right threshold cover had been fitted with a new fastener. Six straps lay in the tool basket, with a third one clipped to the handle of each cart.
storyParagraphsZh: 晚上九点，社区科学展还有半小时撤场，借来的投影仪第二天上午必须还给青少年中心。志愿者叶琳和高宇各装好一辆同型号手推车，每车六块折叠展板，载荷相近，准备从大厅双开门并排推去储藏间。清单写着“平地两条绑带；过不平处建议加第三条”。两人各自拉紧两条绑带，晃了晃最外侧展板，都没有去拿墙边的第三条。
场务把两扇门同时撑住，让两车各沿正对自己的门扇直推，免得临时转弯碰撞。两侧金属门槛盖板表面都平整，白天也一直有人经过。叶琳的左轮压过去，只震了一下；几乎同时，高宇右侧前轮压上另一块盖板，盖板一角忽然翘起，车轮被顶偏。六块展板向右压去，最外一块滑出绑带，撞到门边等待归还的投影仪箱。
场务先封住右侧门扇，再抬起那块盖板。下面一枚固定片已经松脱，表面看不出来，空车经过时也没有翘起；承重车轮压到边缘才把盖板顶起来。高宇把展板扶回车上，随后和场务拍照、登记设备编号。投影仪外壳裂了，镜头座也歪了，第二天原定的课程只能先借备用机。
第二天，高宇按事故记录把投影仪送到维修点，主办方用活动保险办理报修；借用合同仍由主办方承担。几天里，青少年中心来问进度时常直接找高宇，因为设备状况和事故照片都在他手里。与此同时，下次活动有人先问叶琳能不能继续负责贵重设备，也有人在群里把高宇叫成“那次把投影仪撞坏的人”。
叶琳没有替谁下结论。她把撤场时拍到的两辆推车照片发进设备群：两车都只有两条绑带。场务随后补上传了门槛盖板拆开后的照片和维修单。下一次排班表上，叶琳仍在设备搬运栏，高宇却被排到普通布置；高宇照旧去取修好的投影仪，因为他已经和维修公司约好了时间。
一周后，青少年中心签收投影仪。高宇把维修回执交回借用文件夹，主办方的保险材料还夹在里面。下一场活动的两辆推车已经停在墙边，右侧门槛盖板换了新的固定件。工具筐里放着六条绑带，两辆车的把手上各扣着第三条。
explanationParagraphs: Moral luck names a tension: we think moral judgment should rest on choices, intentions, and foreseeable risks within an agent’s control, yet actual judgments are often shaped by outcomes or circumstances outside it. Resultant luck asks why similar choices receive different blame, praise, or character judgments when their outcomes differ.

Outcomes still matter. Real harm creates duties of repair, compensation, care, or explanation. Yet contractual responsibility, remedial duties, judgment of the prior choice, and the reputation later attached to a person are distinct. How far outcomes should alter the latter two is the dispute.
explanationParagraphsZh: 道德运气揭示一种张力：我们认为道德评价应依据行动者能够控制的选择、意图与可预见风险，实际判断却常受其无法控制的后果或处境影响。结果运气（resultant luck）关注近似选择为何因结果不同，得到不同的责备、赞扬或人格评价。
结果仍然重要：真实损害会带来修复、赔偿、照顾或说明等现实义务。但合同责任、补救义务、对行动前选择的评价和后来形成的名声并非同一件事。结果应在多大程度上改变后两者，正是争论所在。
articles.overallZh: 叶琳和高宇在行动前面对近似的信息、目的和风险，并在彼此不知道结果时作出同样的两条绑带选择。真正分开结果的是事前不可见、承重时才显现的门槛盖板故障。高宇因此实际多承担维修与联系工作，但设备损坏又进一步改变了别人对谁更可靠的回看。
articles.overall: Ye Lin and Gao Yu face similar information, purposes, and risks before acting, and both choose two straps before either knows the result. What separates the outcomes is a threshold-cover fault that could not be seen beforehand and appears only under load. Gao Yu therefore takes on more repair and follow-up work in practice, while the damaged projector also changes how others look back on who is more reliable.

moduleZh.intro: 同一次搬运之后，几件事沿不同方向展开：投影仪需要修，借用手续需要完成，当晚的绑带选择仍要按当时信息评价，而活动圈里又产生了关于‘谁更稳’的印象。道德运气关注的正是这些层次怎样被同一个偶然后果拉开。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 偶然后果怎样拉开现实负担与对人的评价
diagramSteps: 先让行动前可控制的信息、意图和可预见风险尽量可比
不可合理预见的后续条件使近似选择产生不同结果
实际损害形成修复、合同或行政上的现实负担
结果进一步渗入对原选择和人格可靠性的回看
在不否认损害的前提下重新区分这些评价层次
diagramStepNotes: 两人同时装车、同时决定只用两条绑带、各沿正对门扇直推，没有顺序模仿或自行选择更险路线的差异。
右侧盖板下的固定片从表面看不见，白天空车经过也无异常；承重车轮压到边缘时，盖板才突然翘起。
维修、备用设备、保险和归还都对应真实发生的损害，因此故事没有把结果说成道德或实践上无关。
借用合同由主办方承担；高宇跟进进度，是因为设备记录和事故照片在他手里。行政安排说明谁把后续事情做完，却没有单独回答原选择和人格该怎样评价。
后续排班和称呼却开始把事故结果转化为‘谁更可靠’的人格评价，这正是故事保留而不替读者裁决的张力。
mapping: 同型号推车、近似载荷、同一清单和同时两条绑带选择 → 行动前可控制条件尽量可比。
右侧门槛隐藏固定片承重后翘起 → 结果差异来自事前不可合理预见的因果因素。
高宇持续跑维修、主办方处理保险合同 → 实际损害确实创造补救与行政负担。
叶琳继续被安排搬贵重设备、高宇被调去普通布置 → 结果开始改变对可靠性和人格的追溯评价。
门槛修好且第三条绑带进入工具筐 → 可以从结果改变未来制度，而不必先把偶然后果全部写回原行动者品格。
moduleZh.boundary: 道德运气不意味着结果完全不重要，也不要求相似行为在所有层面受到相同处理。真实损害会改变修复、赔偿、照顾和行政责任。本故事只聚焦 resultant luck：当行动前的信息、意图与可预见风险近似时，不可控制的结果应在多大程度上进一步改变对原选择或人格的评价。故事中的社区活动与人物均为虚构。
moduleZh.reflection: 为什么高宇实际需要继续处理维修和归还，却不能仅凭这台投影仪真的坏了，就直接推出他当初比叶琳更鲁莽或更不可靠？

module.intro: After the same moving job, several things unfold in different directions: the projector needs repair, the borrowing paperwork must be completed, the strap choice can still be judged by what was known at the time, and the event group forms new impressions about who is dependable. Moral luck asks how one chance outcome pulls these layers apart.
module.diagramTitle: How a chance outcome separates practical burdens from judgments about a person
diagramSteps: Make the controllable information, intentions, and foreseeable risks before action as comparable as possible
An unforeseeable later condition gives similar choices different outcomes
Real harm creates practical repair, contractual, or administrative burdens
The outcome then seeps into retrospective judgments of the choice and the person’s reliability
Re-separate these levels of evaluation without denying the reality of the harm
diagramStepNotes: Both volunteers load at the same time, choose two straps before either sees a result, and push straight through the door directly ahead; there is no imitation sequence or self-chosen riskier route.
The loose fastener under the right-hand cover could not be seen from the surface, and empty carts had crossed without trouble. The cover lifted only when a loaded wheel pressed near its edge.
Repair, backup equipment, insurance, and return procedures all respond to actual damage, so the story does not treat the outcome as morally or practically irrelevant.

The organizer remains responsible for the borrowing contract. Gao Yu follows the repair because he holds the equipment record and incident photos. That arrangement determines who completes the follow-up work, while leaving judgment of the original choice and character as separate questions.
Later rosters and labels begin turning the accident outcome into a judgment about who is “more reliable,” preserving the philosophical tension rather than settling it for the reader.
mapping: Identical carts, similar loads, the same checklist, and simultaneous two-strap choices → the controllable pre-action conditions are kept as comparable as possible.
The hidden fastener under the right threshold cover lifts only under load → the outcome difference comes from a causal factor that was not reasonably foreseeable beforehand.
Gao Yu continues handling the repair while the organizer handles the insurance and contract → actual harm creates genuine remedial and administrative burdens.
Ye Lin remains assigned to valuable equipment while Gao Yu moves to general setup → the outcome begins to alter retrospective judgments of reliability and character.

The threshold is repaired and the third strap is placed in the tool basket → people can change future practice in response to the accident without first writing the accidental outcome entirely back into the agent’s character.
module.boundary: Moral luck does not mean that outcomes are completely irrelevant, nor that similar actions must be treated identically in every respect. Real harm can change duties of repair, compensation, care, and administration. This story focuses only on resultant luck: when pre-action information, intentions, and foreseeable risks are similar, how far should an uncontrollable outcome further alter judgments of the original choice or of the person’s character? The community event and characters are fictional.
module.reflection: Why can Gao Yu genuinely need to keep handling the repair and return of the projector without the fact that it was damaged, by itself, proving that he was more reckless or less reliable than Ye Lin beforehand?

referencesZh.citation: Williams, B. (1981). Moral Luck. In Moral Luck: Philosophical Papers 1973–1980 (pp. 20–39). Cambridge University Press. https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9781139165860.003
referencesZh.use: 用于支持道德评价与行动者控制之间的经典张力，以及结果等运气因素如何进入我们对行动与行动者的评价；不为虚构事故提供事实依据。

referencesZh.use: 用于支持 moral luck 的主要分类与争议，尤其是 resultant luck，并区分控制条件、实际后果与不同层次的道德责任。

references.use: Used to support the classic tension between moral evaluation and an agent’s control, including the way outcomes and other forms of luck enter judgments of actions and agents; it does not provide factual support for the fictional accident.
